messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Bengali, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Bengali line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
আমি যখন তাকে বিশাল মরুভূমিতে দেখলাম, আমি তাকে ডাকলাম যে সে আমার প্রতি দয়া করুক, যাই হোক তুমি ছায়া হোক বা সত্যিকারের মানুষ হোক।

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Bengali) | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------------------|--------| | Quando | “when” (temporal subordinator) | যখন | when | OK | | vidi | “saw” (past, transitive) | দেখলাম | saw | OK | | costui | “him” (demonstrative pronoun) | তাকে | him | OK | | nel | “in” (preposition) | — *(case suffix ‑তে on “মরুভূমি” covers it)* | — | UNNECESSARY | | gran | “great” (attribute) | বিশাল | great | OK | | diserto | “desert” (noun) | মরুভূমি | desert | OK | | Miserere | “have pity” (imperative) | দয়া করুক | may have pity | OK | | di | “on / toward” (preposition) | প্রতি | toward | OK | | me | “me” (object pronoun) | আমার | my (object) | OK | | gridi | “I cried / shouted” (past) | ডাকলাম | called / shouted | OK | | a | “to” (preposition) | — *(dative case on “তাকে” already expresses it)* | — | UNNECESSARY | | lui | “him” (object of preposition) | — *(encoded in “তাকে”)* | — | UNNECESSARY | | qual | “whatever” (free relative) | যাই | whatever | OK | | che | “that / which” (relative linker) | — *(no separate word needed in Bengali)* | — | UNNECESSARY | | tu | “you” (2nd sg pronoun) | তুমি | you | OK | | sii | “be” (subjunctive, 2nd sg) | হোক | be | OK | | od (1) | “or” (first disjunction) | বা | or | OK | | ombra | “shade” (noun) | ছায়া | shade | OK | | od (2) | “or” (second disjunction) | বা | or | OK | | omo | “man” (noun) | মানুষ | man | OK | | certo | “certain / real” (adjective) | সত্যিকারের | real / certain | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `nel`, `a`, `lui`, `che` – Bengali does not need separate prepositions or relative particles here; their functions are expressed by case marking or are implicit. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Bengali script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Bengali text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 64** - Original: আমি যখন তাকে বিশাল মরুভূমিতে দেখলাম, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- **Line 65** - Original: আমি তাকে ডাকলাম যে সে আমার প্রতি দয়া করুক, - Issue: WRONG – the imperative “Miserere di me” is not rendered; the verb “ডাকলাম” (called) is inappropriate. - Corrected: আমি তাকে চিৎকার করে বললাম, “আমার প্রতি দয়া করো!”,
- **Line 66** - Original: যাই হোক তুমি ছায়া হোক বা সত্যিকারের মানুষ হোক। - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
